questions.question_text:
A loan of $\$22\,000$ is taken at $9\%$ p.a. over $3$ years ($36$ months).
Using the repayment table value of $\$31.80$ per $\$1000$ borrowed, calculate the monthly repayment.

options.why: Multiplied table value by $2.2$ instead of $22$ ($22\,000 / 1000$).
Multiplied table value by the full principal $\$22\,000$ instead of per $\$1000$.
Used the $60$-month rate of $\$20.76$ instead of the $36$-month rate.
Read the $12$-month column ($\$88.85$) without converting $2$ years into $24$ months.
Used the $36$-month rate ($\$33.21$) for $3$ years instead of $2$ years.
Used the $8\%$ interest rate table value ($\$45.23$) instead of the $12\%$ value.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Term in months} = 2 \times 12 = 24$
$\text{Table rate (}12\%\text{ p.a., } 24\text{ months)} = \$47.07$
$\text{Monthly repayment} = 47.07 \times \frac{\$16\,000}{1000}$
$= 47.07 \times 16$
$= \$753.12$

questions.question_text:
A $\$18\,000$ loan at $8\%$ p.a. over $4$ years ($48$ months) has a monthly repayment rate of $\$24.41$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.
Calculate the total interest paid over the term of the loan.

options.why: Gave the total amount repaid instead of the total interest paid.
Multiplied the monthly repayment by $4$ years instead of $48$ months before subtracting principal.
Calculated interest using the $5$-year ($60$-month) repayment rate.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the monthly repayment**
$\text{Monthly} = 24.41 \times 18 = \$439.38$
2. **Calculate the total amount repaid**
$\text{Total repaid} = 48 \times \$439.38 = \$21\,090.24$
3. **Calculate the total interest**
$\text{Interest} = \$21\,090.24 - \$18\,000$
$= \$3090.24$

questions.question_text:
A borrower takes a $\$25\,000$ loan at $11\%$ p.a. over $5$ years ($60$ months), where the table rate is $\$21.74$ per $\$1000$.
What is the total amount repaid on the loan?

options.why: Calculated only the total interest paid instead of the total amount repaid.
Multiplied monthly repayment by $50$ months instead of $60$ months.
Added a flat estimated interest without computing exact repayments.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Calculate the monthly repayment**
$\text{Monthly repayment} = 21.74 \times 25 = \$543.50$
2. **Calculate the total amount repaid**
$\text{Total repaid} = 60 \times \$543.50$
$= \$32\,610.00$

options.why: Calculated the difference in monthly repayments rather than total interest.
Gave the total interest of the $5$-year loan without subtracting the $3$-year loan interest.
Gave the total interest of the $3$-year loan instead of the difference.

questions.question_text: For a $\$15\,000$ loan over $4$ years ($48$ months), what is the difference in monthly repayments between an $8\%$ p.a. loan (rate $\$24.41$) and a $14\%$ p.a. loan (rate $\$27.33$)?

questions.question_text:
Daniel can afford at most $\$550$ per month in repayments for a car loan over $5$ years at $8\%$ p.a. (table rate $\$20.28$ per $\$1000$).
The car costs $\$34\,000$.
What is the minimum cash deposit required to keep his loan repayments within budget?

options.why: Calculated the maximum loan amount instead of the required cash deposit.
Estimated a rounded deposit without computing exact decimal values from the rate.
Subtracted an approximate loan figure of $\$28\,000$ from $\$34\,000$.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the repayment rate per $\$1000$ from the table**
$\frac{P}{1000} = \frac{\$550}{20.28} \approx 27.1203155$
$P = 27.1203155 \times 1000 = \$27\,120.32$
2. **Calculate the monthly repayment**
$\text{Minimum deposit} = \$34\,000 - \$27\,120.32$
$= \$6879.68$
